spans.s:
Ulmuka is the common word in the Brāhmaṇas^1 for ‘fire-
brand,’ from which a coal (aṅgāra)^2 could be taken.
1) Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, ii. 11; Sata-
patha Brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 2, 1; ii. 1, 4,
28, etc.; Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa, ii. 76
(Journal of the American Oriental Society,
15, 239)
2) Satapatha Brāhmaṇa, xii. 4, 3, 3;
Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 61, 1 (Journal
of the American Oriental Society, 23,
342).

Ulmukavakṣayaṇa is an expression that occurs several
times in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa,^1 signifying a ‘means of
extinguishing (ava-kṣayaṇa) a firebrand,’ or possibly more pre-
cisely ‘tongs.’ Compare Aṅgārāvakṣayaṇa.
1) iv. 6. 8, 7; v. 2, 4, 15; xi. 6, 3, 3; Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa, ii. 76. Cf. Böhtlingk,
Dictionary, s.v.
